ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black) surface with approximately 15-20% high-intensity (white) pixel coverage concentrated at distal tips and inferior margins.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white regions are mapped to the distal tips of both lobes. The viewer-left lobe features a significant white patch on the inferior-lateral margin. Numerous high-contrast white punctate spots are distributed across the black medial surfaces of both lobes.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped central notch with a depth-to-width ratio indicating a sharp angular depression of approximately 50-60 degrees.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration pattern along the entire trailing boundary; peaks and valleys exhibit variable pixel-amplitudes between 5-12 pixels, creating a jagged, irregular edge profile.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge follows a concave sweep from the median notch toward the distal tips, while the overall fluke geometry displays a convex inferior margin.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, roughly circular clusters of high-intensity pixels corresponding to barnacle colonies are concentrated at the extreme distal tips and along the superior-lateral edges of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A series of thin, dark, non-parallel linear disruptions are visible traversing the white pigmentation patch on the lower section of the viewer-left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A distinct yellowish-brown organic discoloration is present within the high-intensity white area on the inferior portion of the viewer-left lobe. Significant barnacle encrustation is present on the outer lobe tips.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique 'salt-and-pepper' speckling pattern localized in the dark medial region of the viewer-right lobe.
